items.title: Monjasa seals biggest-ever fleet deal with five-tanker swoop
points: Danish bunker supplier and shipowner Monjasa has acquired five sister product tankers from Germany’s Bernhard Schulte in its largest-ever fleet deal, strengthening its marine fuels operations in West Africa.
The Fredericia-based group has picked up five 2010- and 2011-built tankers of around 16,500 dwt each.
Four vessels, renamed Monjasa Tracer, Monjasa Tuner, Monjasa Twister and Monjasa Tracker, have already joined the fleet and are trading in West Africa and Northwest Europe.
The fifth, Monjasa Trigger, is set to follow by the end of November.
The ships previously traded as Eva Schulte, Erika Schulte, Everhard Schulte, Edzard Schulte and Elisabeth Schulte, respectively.
The acquisition takes Monjasa’s owned fleet to 20 tankers, alongside around 10 ships on time charter.

The tankers will initially support Monjasa’s West African operations, although the company also sees opportunities to employ them in commercial freight trading and elsewhere in its global supply network.

items.title: Elemental Energies wins offshore CCS deal from Harbour Energy
points: Aberdeen-based well engineering specialist Elemental Energies has secured a two-year contract from Harbour Energy to support the expansion of the Viking carbon capture and storage (CCS) project in the UK southern North Sea.
The contract covers integrated subsurface, geomechanics and well engineering studies for the Viking East and Viking West storage sites.
Harbour Energy is developing Viking CCS and holds a 60% operating interest, alongside BP with 40%.
The project aims to transport and permanently store carbon dioxide captured from industrial facilities in the Humber region.
Its initial phase is designed to store up to 4m tonnes of CO₂ annually from the early 2030s, with Harbour targeting capacity of up to 15m tonnes per year by 2035.

The development plans to reuse existing southern North Sea infrastructure, including an offshore pipeline linking the former Theddlethorpe gas terminal to depleted Viking gas reservoirs approximately 2.7 km beneath the seabed.
Viking completed front-end engineering design in 2025 and secured development consent for its onshore pipeline the same year.

items.title: India equity mutual fund fund inflows cool as stocks sink to 18-month low
points: Inflows into Indian equity mutual funds slowed in October as investors grew more cautious toward riskier parts of the stock market, curbing exposure to funds that invest in smaller companies.
Equity funds attracted a net ₹33,000 crore (~$3.5 billion), down 14% from ₹38,310 crore in September, according to data from the Association of Mutual Funds in India, or AMFI.
Mutual funds in India pool money from individual investors and invest it across stocks and other assets.

The slowdown came as a selloff pushed the NSE Nifty 50 Index to its lowest since April 2025 early in the month, while rising energy prices due to the war in the Middle East added to inflation concerns.
Small-cap funds attracted 64.1 billion rupees in October, down from a record 90.4 billion rupees in September, while mid-cap inflows fell to 48.9 billion rupees from 78.3 billion rupees.

items.title: Ex-YSRCP leader V Vijaya Sai Reddy launches new party in AP, attacks Jagan’s ‘arrogance’
points: Former YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) leader V Vijaya Sai Reddy on Wednesday launched the Parivarthana Rajaneethi Party (PRP), positioning the new regional political outfit as an alternative to the YSR Congress and the ruling Telugu Desam Party (TDP).
The former Rajya Sabha MP unveiled his new political party at a convention centre in Vijayawada at 11.11 am, saying he chose the date and time on astrologers’ advice.
Sai Reddy was among those who stood by his mentor’s son, YS Jagan Mohan Reddy, when he left the Congress and founded the YSR Congress in 2010.

Sai Reddy was elected to the Rajya Sabha in 2016, got a second term in 2023, and was the YSR Congress’s parliamentary party leader until January 2025, when he resigned from the Rajya Sabha and left the party after differences with Jagan.
The former MP launched a sharp attack on the YSRCP, pointing to its sharp decline from 151 seats in the 175-member assembly in 2019 to just 11 seats in the 2024 elections.

items.title: India eyes wind turbine upgrades to boost output, overcome land hurdles
points: India is weighing replacing aging wind turbines with larger, more efficient machines to boost generation at older farms without having to acquire more land.

As much as 8 gigawatts of capacity using old and smaller turbines can be upgraded with modern units, according to a preliminary assessment by the Indian Wind Turbine Manufacturers Association, Chief Executive Officer Aditya Pyasi said in an interview.
The lobby group is in talks with federal and state governments to finalize a plan that could help increase capacity at those sites by almost 50%.

Although the country’s green power capacity has quadrupled since 2014, wind installations have lagged far behind solar, with land acquisition and securing right-of-way remaining major hurdles to faster deployment.
Still, wind project deployment remains below the pace needed to meet India’s 2030 goal of 500 gigawatts clean power capacity.
Replacing older turbines of as much as 2 megawatts with modern 3- to 5-megawatt units at existing sites could help sidestep land-access hurdles.

items.title: Firecrackers still Delhi’s top pollutant after Deepavali, IITM finds
points: The contribution of firecrackers to the city's pollution levels was significantly higher on Monday (November 9), a day after Deepavali, before declining on Tuesday (November 11), the IITM models showed.

The estimates had a standard deviation (SD) of 104.1 percentage points on Monday (November 9) and 27.7 percentage points on Tuesday (November 10), indicating considerable variability and uncertainty in the modelled contributions.
On Monday (November 9), vehicular emissions accounted for 6.9% of the pollution, followed by secondary inorganic aerosols at 5% and secondary organic aerosols at 4.5%.
Mixed or unresolved biofuel contributed 4.45%, while mineral dust and ash and mixed combustion accounted for 2.5% each.
Wood burning contributed 1.3%, while waste burning, including municipal and plastic-rubber-containing waste, accounted for 1.1%.
On Tuesday (November 10), the contribution of firecrackers dropped to 29.8%, while secondary organic aerosols emerged as the second-largest contributor at 17.5%.
Delhi's average 24-hour Air Quality Index (AQI) had improved marginally to the 'poor' category on Tuesday (November 10), with the 4 p.m. reading settling at 299.

The chief minister’s remarks come against the backdrop of concerns in Lucknow and other parts of the state over the thick blanket of acrid smoke on Diwali night and a midnight road visibility of just 200 metres following unrestricted bursting of firecrackers.
Since 2015, Lucknow’s air has been worse the day after Diwali than the day before, according to the CPCB 4pm bulletins.

The air quality index (AQI) in Lucknow, which has six monitoring stations, rose from 207 on November 7 to 233 on November 8 and 245 on November 9 before winds dispersed the pollutants and helped bring back the AQI to a moderate’ 172 on Tuesday.
On Diwali, AQI in Ghaziabad was 344 (’very poor’), Noida 318 (very poor), Greater Noida 299 (poor) and Meerut 295 (poor).

points: The Kolkata-Sairang Express derailment near Digaru railway station in Assam's Kamrup (Metropolitan) district on Wednesday left passengers shaken, with a crew member describing how the train continued travelling for nearly a kilometre after going off the…

When the train arrived at Digaru Station, it slowed down a little.

items.title: Siemens’ growth pipeline is strong. Can margins keep pace?
points: Siemens’ strong order pipeline in the September quarter (Q2FY27), healthy execution and improving sequential margins suggest that the capital expenditure cycle is gathering momentum.

items.title: Odisha Scraps OCS Exam Attempt Limit; General, SEBC Candidates Get Unlimited Chances
points: The Odisha government has decided to remove the limit on the number of attempts candidates can make to appear for the Odisha Civil Services (OCS) examination.
The decision was approved during a State Cabinet meeting held on November 9, 2026.
The meeting was chaired by Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi.
As per the official press release, the Cabinet has approved amendments to the Odisha Civil Services (Combined Competitive Recruitment Examination) Rules, 1991.
Under the new rules, candidates will be able to appear for the OCS examination as many times as they wish.

General category candidates could appear for the examination only six times, while candidates belonging to the Socially and Educationally Backward Classes (SEBC) category were allowed a maximum of nine attempts.
However, candidates should remember that the removal of the attempt limit does not mean the removal of the age limit.

points: Panic ensued at Kolkata's Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport on Wednesday morning following reports of a hijack threat directed at a Mumbai-bound Air India flight.

According to reports, the aircraft was preparing for takeoff when the threatening message on the lavatory mirror was noticed.
Upon learning of the incident, the pilot immediately alerted Air Traffic Control (ATC).
The aircraft was subsequently moved to an isolation bay, where the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) and specialised airport security personnel launched an intensive search operation.
Every part of the aircraft is being thoroughly examined to detect the presence of any suspicious items.
Police and security agencies have initiated an investigation to determine who wrote the threatening message and who might be behind it.
Authorities are currently reviewing the footage from CCTV cameras located within the airport premises and inside the aircraft.
